<objective>
Close the four verification spikes the Phase 2 runner design depends on, as a committed, re-runnable probe suite plus a generated, version-stamped findings document — not one-time hand-written notes.

Purpose: the reason SPIKE-01 through SPIKE-04 are open is that the `claude` CLI's flag set and stream-json schema are explicitly not stable contracts. A probe that can be re-run after a CLI upgrade turns "a fact silently drifted" from a mystery runner failure in Phase 2 into a test failure here. Phase 1 success criterion 4 is exactly this.
Output: `src/spikes/` containing a hermetic SPIKE-01 classifier that runs in the default suite, three real-CLI probes behind an opt-in `npm run spikes` target, and `01-SPIKE-FINDINGS.md` recording the answers against a specific `claude --version`.
</objective>

<user_story>
**As a** developer about to build a runner on top of four unverified CLI facts,
**I want to** re-run a committed probe suite after any `claude` upgrade and get a versioned findings document,
**so that** a silently changed flag value or event schema surfaces as a red test instead of as an agent session that mysteriously never starts.
</user_story>

  <behavior>
    - A `system` event with subtype `api_retry` and `error` of `rate_limit` classifies as `rate_limit`.
    - The same shape with `error` of `billing_error` classifies as `billing_error`; with `overloaded` classifies as `overloaded`.
    - The same shape with any other member of the documented error enum (`authentication_failed`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `invalid_request`, `model_not_found`, `server_error`, `max_output_tokens`, `unknown`) classifies as `other_error`.
    - An `assistant`, `user`, `stream_event` or successful `result` event classifies as null.
    - A `rate_limit_event` line with `status` of `rejected` classifies as `rate_limit`; with `allowed_warning` classifies as `rate_limit_warning`; with `allowed` classifies as null.
    - A line whose `type` is a string not in the documented set classifies as `unknown` and does not throw.
    - A line that is not valid JSON, is null, or is a bare string classifies as `unknown` and does not throw.
    - `classifyRun({ exitCode, stdoutLines, stderr, versionString })` reports `suspected: true` when the exit code is non-zero, or a `result` event carries a subtype other than `success`, or any line classifies as `rate_limit` or `rate_limit_warning`, or stderr contains limit wording — and `suspected: false` only when none fire.
    - `classifyRun` reports which of the four signals fired, so an ambiguous case is distinguishable from an unambiguous one, and biases to `suspected: true` on any single hit.
    - `captureEvidence` writes a file containing the full unmodified stdout and stderr buffers, the version string, an ISO-8601 timestamp, and the fired-signal list, and returns the path.
  </behavior>
  <action>
Write `src/spikes/rate-limit-classifier.test.ts` first, one case per `<behavior>` bullet, driven entirely by hand-constructed JSON fixtures in `src/spikes/fixtures/stream-events.ts`. This file lives under `src/spikes/` but is named `.test.ts` rather than `.spike.test.ts`, so per Plan 01's vitest project configuration it runs inside the default hermetic `unit` project and never spawns a process — D-10 is explicit that the classifier's correctness against documented shapes is testable without burning a plan window. Confirm the suite is red before implementing.

`src/spikes/rate-limit-classifier.ts` exports `LimitSignal` as the union `'rate_limit' | 'rate_limit_warning' | 'billing_error' | 'overloaded' | 'other_error' | 'unknown'`, and `classifyStreamEvent(line: unknown): LimitSignal | null`. Accept either a raw string or an already-parsed value; parse defensively inside a try/catch and return `unknown` on any failure. Match the documented shapes from CLAUDE.md § A2: a `type` of `system` with `subtype` of `api_retry` reads the `error` field against the documented enum, and a `type` of `rate_limit_event` reads its `status` field. Any `type` that is a string but is not one of the documented values returns `unknown` rather than throwing — CLAUDE.md § A2 states this explicitly, and it is the exact construct that broke the SDK's own consumers when `rate_limit_event` appeared. Read numeric fields (`attempt`, `max_retries`, `retry_delay_ms`, `error_status`) without coercing an absent field to zero, so a missing field is distinguishable from a zero value.

`classifyRun(input)` implements SAFE-05's multi-signal combination over a whole run and returns `{ suspected, firedSignals, perLineSignals }`. The four signals are: a non-zero process exit code; a `result` event whose `subtype` is not `success`; any line whose `classifyStreamEvent` result is `rate_limit` or `rate_limit_warning`; and a case-insensitive substring match on limit wording in stderr, used as a last-resort fallback only. Bias toward suspicion — any single signal firing sets `suspected` true, because the cost of pausing unnecessarily is a delay while the cost of missing a limit is a busy-retry loop against an exhausted window. Record which signals fired rather than collapsing to a boolean, since Phase 2's queue-pause logic and the findings document both need to know how strong the evidence was.

`src/spikes/evidence-trap.ts` exports `captureEvidence({ stdout, stderr, versionString, firedSignals })`, which writes an evidence file under `<fleetHome>/spike-evidence/` named with an ISO-8601 timestamp, containing the complete unmodified buffers, and returns its path. This is D-10's trap: SPIKE-01 cannot be forced on demand without burning the plan window this project exists to conserve, so instead the detector ships now and the next genuine rate-limit encounter — in real Phase 2 or later use — captures ground truth for free. Do not redact or truncate the buffers; the whole value of the trap is fidelity.
  </action>

  <action>
Build the shared probe infrastructure first, then the three probes. Every file here is named `.spike.test.ts` so it matches Plan 01's `spike` vitest project glob and is excluded from the default `unit` project — D-11 requires `npm test` to stay fast, hermetic, and runnable with no CLI auth.

`src/spikes/spawn-claude.ts` exports `CLAUDE_ENV_ALLOWLIST`, an explicit array of the variable names a spawned `claude` may see — `HOME`, `PATH`, `USER`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL`, `TERM`, `TMPDIR`, `SHELL`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` — and `spawnClaude(args, { cwd, stdin })` which builds the child environment by copying only those keys from `process.env` into a fresh object. Build up from an allowlist; never start from the inherited environment and delete known-bad keys, because a denylist is provably incomplete and these probes are exactly the "just testing, doesn't matter" code that historically becomes the leak vector. Spawn with an argv array, never a shell string, and never through a login shell. Return the exit code, the stdout lines, and the stderr buffer. Also export `claudeVersion()` returning the trimmed `claude --version` output, which every probe result must carry per D-12.

`src/spikes/scratch-repo.ts` exports `withScratchRepo(fn)`, which creates a temp directory, runs `git init` and one empty commit in it, invokes the callback with the path, and removes the directory in a finally block. Every probe that spawns `claude` runs inside a scratch repo produced here and never inside a registered project's checkout or the Fleet repository itself. This is not hygiene — a target repo's own `.claude/settings.json` carrying an `apiKeyHelper` or `env` block would be read by the CLI and could silently flip billing off the subscription, which is the highest-cost failure mode this project has.
